resources.string: Relative example, not a measurement. Thin and thick filaments slide past one another; their own lengths remain unchanged.
Z-disc distance: %1$d%% of the relaxed example
Rose: thin filaments · violet: thick filaments
A widened process contacts the outer surface of a small blood vessel.
Branches contact the local environment around neurons and synapses.
A myelinating Schwann cell wraps one segment of a peripheral axon.
The Schwann cell nucleus lies outside the compact myelin layers.
Aligned sarcomeres create repeating bands in a skeletal muscle fibre.
This long, multinucleated fibre has nuclei near its surface.
The marked boundary depicts a junction with a neighbouring cardiac cell. These junctions couple the cells mechanically and electrically.
A cardiac muscle cell usually has a centrally located nucleus.
Branches allow individual cardiac cells to connect into a network.
The cell narrows toward each end and does not show the repeating striations seen in skeletal muscle.
A single elongated nucleus usually runs along the centre of the cell.
Keratin filaments help a living epidermal cell withstand mechanical stress.
Adhesive contacts link a keratinocyte to neighbouring cells.
Processes deliver pigment-containing material to neighbouring keratinocytes.
Fibroblasts can have an elongated body within connective tissue.
Fibroblasts build extracellular material, including collagen fibres.
The representative white adipocyte stores much of its lipid in one large droplet.
The large lipid droplet displaces the nucleus to the edge.
An osteoblast on a bone surface deposits new organic matrix.
The newly deposited organic matrix later mineralizes.
A mature osteocyte occupies a small space in mineralized bone.
Tiny channels accommodate cell processes that connect the osteocyte with its surroundings.
A mature osteoclast has several nuclei after fusion of precursor cells.
Folds face the bone surface at an active area of bone resorption.
A chondrocyte sits inside a small cavity in the cartilage matrix.
The surrounding matrix contains water and macromolecules and supports the tissue under load.
A thin layer of endothelial cells lines the inside of a vessel.
The nuclear region is thicker than the very thin parts of an endothelial cell.
Hepatocytes form closely packed plates; the diagram shows one representative cell and its neighbours.
A tiny channel between adjacent hepatocytes carries secreted bile towards the ducts.
Dense microvilli increase the absorptive surface on the intestinal side.
The basal side faces the underlying tissue; it is not the intestinal lumen.
A cap at the tip of the head covers part of the sperm nucleus.
The midpiece contains mitochondria arranged around the base of the flagellum.
Bending of the flagellum moves the cell.
A glycoprotein layer surrounds the oocyte outside its plasma membrane.
A small polar body can lie between the oocyte and the zona pellucida after an asymmetric meiotic division.
A layer of supporting cells surrounds the zona pellucida in this representative view.
